title: IONQ Stock Soars 22% As Company Deploys One Of Europe’s Largest Operational Quantum Key Distribution Networks
key_facts: IonQ announced that it has deployed one of the largest operational quantum key distribution (QKD) networks in Europe.
The network powers the Romanian National Quantum Communication Infrastructure, described as one of the largest QKD networks outside China.
IonQ delivered it with the National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest and Romania's national research and education network.
The network is built only on IonQ's commercially available QKD technology; IonQ says this shows quantum-secure communications are scalable and operational for national infrastructure.
IonQ CEO Niccolo de Masi said it supports security initiatives across government, healthcare, research, education and data center environments.
IonQ says the network spans more than 1,500 kilometers, a fifth of Europe's terrestrial quantum communications infrastructure.
Shares rose more than 22% in Thursday's opening trade; the article says IonQ reported fourth-quarter earnings the day before.
quote_evidence: The company stated that its technology powers the Romanian National Quantum Communication Infrastructure, one of the largest quantum key distribution (QKD) networks outside of China.
The firm added that Romania’s quantum infrastructure now spans more than 1,500 kilometers, accounting for a fifth of Europe’s terrestrial quantum communications infrastructure to date.
IonQ reported its fourth-quarter (Q4) earnings on Wednesday, beating Wall Street estimates in terms of both earnings and revenue.
why_it_matters_hint: A working national network of quantum-protected links is the kind of infrastructure governments and hospitals could use for sensitive data, but the scale and benefit are IonQ's own statements.
